Implement agent chaining so multiple agents collaborate to solve complex tasks. Develop and refine prompts to maximize the performance and accuracy of language models. Deploy and operate agents on AWS (Bedrock, Lambda, Step Functions or equivalent) with proper logging, monitoring, cost tracking and alerting. Write evaluations that prove an agent is accurate before go-live and keep it accurate afterwards. Apply security and data governance by design: least-privilege access, secrets management, PII handling and audit trails. Track token and infrastructure spend per agent so value can be reported net of cost. Maintain clear and comprehensive technical documentation, and share patterns so the rest of the company can reuse them. Mentor and provide technical guidance to junior Python engineers and team members. Advocate for AI adoption inside the team, inspiring and supporting others. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics or a related field. 4-7 years in software or data engineering, with at least 2 years focused on LLM and agent systems in production. Deep working knowledge of agent design methods: tool use and function calling, planning and orchestration patterns, retrieval (RAG), memory and context management, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop design. Ability to work with different LLM models and choose one over another based on the use case. Strong Python, including building APIs (FastAPI), integrations and data pipelines. Strong SQL and experience working with a cloud data warehouse, ideally Snowflake. Experience deploying and operating services on AWS (or Azure), including serverless, containers, IAM, observability and CI/CD. Experience evaluating LLM systems: test sets, automated evals, regression testing of prompts and models. Builds software in an AI-driven way: AI coding agents, spec-first development, and human review at each stage. Understanding of data privacy, AI ethics, Responsible AI and model governance. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work independently and with a team. Excellent communication skills, with the ability to present complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences. Additional Experience Desired Familiarity with AWS AIDLC or a similar AI-driven development methodology. Experience building MCP servers or Claude skills. AWS Bedrock in production. Snowflake Cortex, dbt or semantic layer modelling. TypeScript in addition to Python. Integration experience with NetSuite, Salesforce, Zendesk or similar business systems. Automating finance, operations or customer support processes. Working in regulated or data-sensitive industries such as legal, financial services or healthcare. Experience with vector databases (FAISS, Pinecone) and Hugging Face. Good understanding of software engineering processes, and experience working with large datasets in production. Contributions to research papers, blogs or open-source projects. Benefits Vacations. Job Description The Performance Management Programs & Insights Specialist helps translate HPE’s Performance Management strategy into integrated execution, actionable insights, and an effective team member and people leader experience. This role coordinates priorities, milestones, dependencies, reporting, system readiness, resources, and continuous-improvement activities across the Performance Management portfolio. The Specialist partners with Performance program owners and cross-functional teams to help deliver global performance cycles and advance data, digital, and AI-enabled capabilities. The ideal candidate combines strong program-management discipline with analytical thinking, curiosity about emerging HR technology, and the ability to turn complex information into clear actions and recommendations. Responsibilities Portfolio and program execution: Maintain an integrated view of Performance Management priorities, milestones, dependencies, risks, capacity considerations, and decision points. Partner with program owners to identify conflicts, support prioritization, and maintain delivery momentum. Project and workstream management: Lead assigned projects or workstreams by defining objectives, scope, success measures, plans, roles, and deliverables. Monitor progress, manage issues, and coordinate stakeholders to support timely, high-quality outcomes. Performance insights and data storytelling: Coordinate Performance Insights, dashboard, reporting, and KPI requirements in partnership with People Analytics, HRIS, and program owners. Analyze adoption, completion, quality, experience, and effectiveness indicators and translate findings into clearly communicated insights and actionable recommendations. Business requirements and system readiness: Help translate business needs into documented requirements, acceptance criteria, and readiness plans. Coordinate business User Acceptance Testing, issue tracking, retesting, sign-off, and launch-readiness activities in partnership with HRIS and HRIT. Digital and AI-enabled transformation: Support the responsible adoption of digital and AI-enabled Performance Management capabilities. Identify opportunities to simplify work, improve user experience, automate recurring activities, and measure adoption and benefits while keeping human judgment and accountability at the center. Resources, enablement, and content quality: Coordinate the development, review, maintenance, and publishing readiness of Performance Management resources, including guides, FAQs, knowledge articles, training materials, and partner-readiness content. Promote consistency, accuracy, accessibility, and a simplified user experience. Program effectiveness and continuous improvement: Use surveys, focus groups, operational feedback, data, and cycle retrospectives to assess program effectiveness. Document lessons learned and recommend practical improvements to processes, resources, systems, and stakeholder experiences. Governance, eligibility, and compliance: Support eligibility validation, audit documentation, access and security coordination, records management, and adherence to applicable global and local requirements. Maintain clear documentation and escalate risks or exceptions to the appropriate program owner. Education And Experience Required First level university degree. Typically, 3+ years of experience in Human Resources, program or project management, people analytics, HR technology, talent management, business transformation, or a related field. Experience coordinating cross-functional projects, programs, or system-enabled process improvements. Direct Performance Management experience is preferred but not required. Experience with HR platforms, reporting or dashboard tools, digital transformation, or AI-enabled solutions is an advantage. Knowledge And Skills Strong program and project management skills, with the ability to organize priorities, manage risks, and drive work forward. Analytical mindset with the ability to turn data into meaningful insights and clear recommendations. Strong communication and presentation skills, with a talent for making complex topics simple and engaging. Interest in digital, AI, automation, and emerging HR technologies, with a passion for exploring new ways of working. Understanding of business requirements, UAT, system readiness, and process implementation. Strong collaboration and relationship-building skills across HR, technology, analytics, and business teams. Creative problem-solving and continuous-improvement mindset, with a focus on simplification and user experience.
